source_text: Quanto rectius diceres: Dixit hoc idem et Manichaeus in epistola ad Patricium; dixit et in epistola quam scripsit ad filiam Menoch, dixit et in aliis multis scriptis, quae tu penitus imbibisti? Sed in consortium tuum episcopum Mediolanensem conaris attrahere, et quia non potes habere praesidium, vis invenire solatium.
pass_a_gloss: How much more rightly would you say: Manichaeus said this same thing in the letter to Patricius; he said it also in the letter which he wrote to his daughter Menoch, he said it also in many other writings, which you have thoroughly drunk in? But you try to drag the bishop of Milan into your fellowship, and because you cannot have protection, you want to find comfort.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS/Blaise range; English follows the Latin without NPNF copy

pass_b_english: How much more rightly you would say: “Manichaeus said the same thing in his letter to Patricius. He also said it in the letter he wrote to his daughter Menoch, and in many other writings that you have thoroughly absorbed.” Instead, you try to draw the bishop of Milan into your company. Because you cannot obtain a defense, you want to find consolation.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
